mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the contracting young Sun was most worthwhile: it clarified that accretion and contraction power its light before sustained hydrogen fusion, while planets can already begin forming.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding rock-forming dust to the existing dusty disk felt somewhat repetitive, even though it completed the goal.

surprise.text: I was interested that planet formation can begin before the Sun reaches sustained main-sequence hydrogen burning.

arbitrary.text: Combining the rotating core with ice-mantled dust to make a disk felt somewhat compressed: the result explains the orbiting material, but the particular pairing did not make the mechanism obvious beforehand.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the disk’s inherited dust and volatile material become planets, especially if the explanations continue to distinguish the underlying processes.
